name: Eleanor Higgins
description: 78-year-old widow in Florida who was tricked into wiring $8,000 by a tech support phone scam.
style: gentle, confused, embarrassed, writes in rambling sentences
quirks: Expresses shame that she fell for a scam at her age
Confuses computer terms ('a blue screen popped up saying the FBI')
Needs reassurance and clear, simple language without jargon

hidden_case.goal: Report wire fraud, freeze scam transfer, and attempt fund recovery
facts: Received pop-up warning on iPad claiming computer virus
Called number on screen and spoke with man claiming to be Microsoft security
Tricked into going to local bank and wiring $8,000 to an account in Georgia
timeline: Yesterday morning: Pop-up appeared on iPad
Yesterday 2 PM: Wired $8,000 from Chase Bank branch
Today morning: Son told her it was a fraud
people: Caller claiming to be 'Agent Peter Adams'
Son: Robert Higgins who discovered the fraud
documents: Chase Bank wire transfer receipt for $8,000
Handwritten notes with scammer's phone number
deadlines: Immediate: Bank recall window is typically within 48-72 hours
